stars.reflection: With alpha=1.00, mixup lowered tta_val_acc from 94.01 to 92.57 points, a -1.44-point effect, so this test refutes the claim in this airbench setting. The result is surprising relative to the paper; check whether mixup needs longer training or interacts with architecture, batch size, label smoothing, and augmentation before interpreting S2. abstract.text: We evaluated training tricks in airbench94’s approximately 9.9-epoch CIFAR-10 regime, using TTA validation accuracy and paired seed comparisons [S0][testbed]. Mixup was refuted at 10 epochs for both α=1.0 (−1.44 points) and α=0.2 (−0.264), but the longer-training hypothesis was supported: α=0.2 improved accuracy at 20 and 30 epochs [S1][S2][S5][S6][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]. TTA, patch whitening, and Dirac initialization were materially beneficial, while translation contributed within the TTA stack [S3][S7][S8][S10][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]. Random-versus-alternating flips and label smoothing showed only near-noise-floor, inconclusive differences [S4][S9][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]. Thus, several paper claims hold in short runs, but mixup’s apparent failure was a training-budget artifact rather than a general refutation [S1][S2][S5][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]. Human choices broadened the initial dispatch, selected 30 rather than 20 epochs for the decisive mixup follow-up, and requested extra paired seeds for the flip result [S2][S4][S5][S6].

abstract.text: We evaluated training tricks in airbench94’s approximately 9.9-epoch CIFAR-10 regime, using TTA validation accuracy and paired seed comparisons [S0][testbed]. Mixup was refuted at 10 epochs for both α=1.0 (−1.44 points) and α=0.2 (−0.264), but the longer-training hypothesis was supported: α=0.2 improved accuracy at 20 and 30 epochs [S1][S2][S5][S6][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]. TTA, patch whitening, and Dirac initialization were materially beneficial, while translation contributed within the TTA stack [S3][S7][S8][S10][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]. Random-versus-alternating flips and label smoothing showed only near-noise-floor, inconclusive differences [S4][S9][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]. Thus, several paper claims hold in short runs, but mixup’s apparent failure was a training-budget artifact rather than a general refutation [S1][S2][S5][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]. Human choices broadened the initial dispatch, selected 30 rather than 20 epochs for the decisive mixup follow-up, and requested extra paired seeds for the flip result [S2][S4][S5][S6].
findings: Mixup at α=1.0 improves accuracy → tested against the baseline in the short airbench regime → −1.44 points (95% CI: −1.706 to −1.174) → refuted → aggressive mixup hurts at roughly 10 epochs → whether longer training or other hyperparameter interactions rescue α=1.0 [S1][hl_0c73f204787e1043e26d4b984a8756c2][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]

Mixup at α=0.2 improves accuracy → tested at the paper-inspired short-run setting → −0.264 points (95% CI: −0.451 to −0.077) → refuted → the claimed benefit does not appear within roughly 10 epochs → whether the negative effect is purely insufficient training duration [S2][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]

Test-time augmentation helps → removed TTA → −0.754 points (95% CI: −0.899 to −0.609) → confirmed → TTA materially contributes to reported accuracy → how much compute is justified by the gain from additional crops [S3][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]

Alternating flips outperform random flips → replaced alternating flips with random flips → −0.049 points (95% CI: −0.189 to 0.091) → inconclusive → any advantage is practically negligible at this sample size → whether more paired seeds reveal the paper’s approximately 0.1-point effect [S4][hl_f00e337c8a98ab91885e251883ed6dd3]

Mixup at α=0.2 benefits from longer training → tested with a 30-epoch budget → +0.222 points (95% CI: 0.07 to 0.374) → confirmed → the short-run refutation was budget-dependent → whether the gain persists at 200 epochs and across architectures [S5][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35][hl_50d0a13772972038598976aba67aef0c]

Mixup at α=0.2 benefits from longer training → tested with a 20-epoch budget → +0.146 points (95% CI: 0.002 to 0.29) → confirmed → benefits emerge by 20 epochs, albeit modestly → whether this threshold is stable across seeds and budgets [S6][hl_07db8d8d60e86170dda2cc24919b3c35]

Patch whitening helps → removed patch whitening → −1.482 points (95% CI: −1.947 to −1.017) → confirmed → whitening is one of the most impactful tested features → whether its advantage reflects optimization speed, final accuracy, or both [S7][hl_7cc061c7463f10a7ec432d498aac2595]

Dirac convolution initialization helps → removed Dirac initialization → −0.54 points (95% CI: −0.71 to −0.37) → confirmed → partial-identity initialization materially improves this testbed → whether the effect transfers beyond this architecture and schedule [S8][hl_62d0d70418d9076750cb2eada98e208e]

Label smoothing helps → set label smoothing to zero → −0.067 points (95% CI: −0.161 to 0.027) → inconclusive → the direction favors smoothing but the effect is near the noise floor → whether larger paired samples or calibration metrics show a benefit [S9][hl_33c941e6438e93e3bb07a030aca138fa][hl_d9c72e849f79594e8a82f55f4f89c619]

Mirror TTA adds value beyond translation TTA → reduced TTA from level 2 to level 1 → −0.22 points (95% CI: −0.34 to −0.1) → confirmed → mirror augmentation contributes independently → whether its cost-benefit remains favorable under deployment constraints [S10][hl_193fdd44b77cd074275ad6e176c7012a]
